errorCodes.meaning: HCP `invalid-token` (HCP 5.5): "Missing, malformed, or expired authorization evidence", here the access token the request presents. A token issued under a revoked grant, a relinquished one included (HCP 5.2.7), fails here too: HCP requires that no request presenting evidence issued under a revoked grant succeeds, but names no error (HCP 6.2.2), and this family reads that evidence as invalid, pending HCP confirmation (question 2). Such a failure is itself a notice of revocation to the client (HCP 6.2.2). Defined once for the family in [the hcp family conventions](/specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).

provenance.description: True where the disclosure carried provenance (HCP 7.4.1); omitted otherwise.

revealed.description: Present only where a credential was disclosed in derived form (HCP 8.2, 14.9). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

items.description: Where a credential was disclosed in derived form, the evidence item and the claims revealed (HCP 14.9).

claims.description: The claims revealed, each a JSON Pointer. The maxItems and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

useUntil.description: The use-until time the disclosure was given (HCP 7.6).

AuditEvent.description: One audit event (HCP 8.2). The log names entries by their stable `id`, never by the `ref` a client received, because the log is the Context Subject's (HCP 8.2, 8.3). The query text is never recorded (HCP 8.2). `entryId`, `relatedEntryId`, `purpose`, `purposeDescription` and `grantId` are required, each a value or null, as HCP 8.2's template writes them: HCP's own shape leaves them optional, and the carriage requires them so that a null always travels and is never confused with an absent member, pending HCP confirmation (question 42). An event redacted for a former delegate carries `entryId` and `relatedEntryId` as null (HCP 17.7).

categories.description: The categories concerned (HCP 8.2). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

data.description: The members HCP 8.2 fixes for the event type, such as `options` for `context.exported` or `ruleId` for `rule.set`. Implementations may add members, which are preserved and not interpreted (HCP 8.2, A.3).

disclosed.description: Present on `context.read`: every entry the retrieval disclosed (HCP 8.2). A retrieval discloses at most 20 entries (HCP 7.2).

entryId.description: The entry concerned, by its `id`, or null where the event concerns none (HCP 8.2). For conflict events, the conflicted entry (HCP 8.2). Required, and null in an event redacted for a former delegate (HCP 17.7), pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

eventType.description: The event type, one of those HCP 8.1 lists (such as `context.read`, `grant.revoked`, `rule.set`). Left open, as HCP's own shape leaves it, so that the event types of a later draft are not refused. The minLength and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

grantId.description: The grant concerned, or null where the event concerns none (HCP 8.2). Required, pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

purpose.description: The purpose code stated, an absolute URI with the same shape as `PurposeCode` in common.schema.json (HCP's `anyOf [purposeCode, null]`), or null where none was (HCP 8.2, 6.1.5.2). `format` constrains only a string, so null still passes. Required, pending HCP confirmation (question 42). The minLength and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

purposeDescription.description: The stated task, or null where none was stated (HCP 8.2). Required, pending HCP confirmation (question 42). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

relatedEntryId.description: For conflict events, the authoritative entry (or the other entry where neither or both are authoritative); null for every other event type (HCP 8.2). Required, and null in an event redacted for a former delegate (HCP 17.7), pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

timestamp.description: When the event occurred. HCP's member name (HCP 8.2), carried verbatim so the event is the one an export carries (HCP 5.4.1).

AuditParticipants.description: The participants in an audit event (HCP 8.2, 3.9). No event names "system" (HCP 8.2).

clientOperator.description: The Client Operator, where a client took part (HCP 3.9).

id.description: Their identifier. The minLength and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

role.description: Their role (HCP 8.2). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

model.description: The model, where one took part (HCP 3.9).

requestingParty.description: The Requesting Party, where there is one (HCP 3.9).

AuditParty.description: A participant named by its identifier (HCP 8.2).

id.description: The participant's identifier. The minLength and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

Category.description: An HCP context category (HCP 4.5), the primary unit of access control: either a slug from HCP's category registry, such as `general_preferences` or `health_context`, or a custom category written as an absolute URI under a domain its definer controls. A custom category is not portable between providers without bilateral agreement (HCP 4.5). The pattern admits the slug or an absolute URI's outline only: it carries no `format: uri`, which would refuse every slug, so checking that a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP's prose requires (HCP A.3), is the consumer's check.

Response.description: One page of the audit log, as the caller may read it (HCP 8.3, 17.7). Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

events.description: The audit events of this page, oldest first (HCP 8.2). HCP 9.4.7 names no member for them; `events` is this carriage's name, pending HCP confirmation (question 30). For a delegate or former delegate, only the events HCP 17.7 lets them read; for a former delegate, `entryId` and `relatedEntryId` are withheld as null and `disclosed` and the `data` of a `context.*` event are left out (HCP 17.7), pending HCP confirmation (question 42). Empty when nothing matches.

nextCursor.description: HCP `nextCursor` (HCP 9.5): an opaque token for the next page, which encodes no credential or entry content and stays valid for at least 300 seconds. Absent, never null, when the result set is exhausted: a departure from HCP 9.5's null, pending HCP confirmation (question 3). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Read Audit Log — response payload

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

schema.description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Read audit log operation (HCP 8.3, 5.4; `GET /v2/audit` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.7, paginated per HCP 9.5): a Management Client, acting for the Context Subject, a delegate or a former delegate, reads one page of the audit log, filtered as asked. HCP defines no request or result schema for this operation; the filters come from HCP 8.3 and the paging members from HCP 9.5. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement. OPTIONAL: where it is absent, the provider authenticates the request's `issuer` VID, by the REQUIRED request proof, as a Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled (HCP 3.2.3), and refuses any other issuer with permissionDenied; where it is present, the token rules apply unchanged. Pending HCP confirmation (question 56).

category.description: Only events whose `categories` include this category (HCP 8.3: "filter by ... category"; the name as in HCP 9.4.12). The member name is this carriage's reading, pending HCP confirmation (question 29).

client.description: Only events in which this HCP Client took part, as initiator or as the client of the grant concerned, by its client identifier (HCP 8.3: "filter by HCP Client"; the name as in HCP 9.4.12). The member name and what it matches are this carriage's reading, pending HCP confirmation (question 29). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

cursor.description: HCP `cursor` (HCP 9.5): the opaque continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`. Absent asks for the first page. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

eventType.description: Only events of this type, one of those HCP 8.1 lists, such as `context.read` (HCP 8.3: "filter by ... event type"; named after the audit event's own `eventType`, HCP 8.2). The member name is this carriage's reading, pending HCP confirmation (question 29). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

from.description: Only events whose `timestamp` is at or after this instant: the lower bound of HCP 8.3's date range (the name as in HCP 9.4.12). Inclusive, pending HCP confirmation (questions 29 and 30).

limit.description: HCP `limit` (HCP 9.5): the most events to return in this page. Absent leaves the page size to the provider. The maximum of 1000 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement (pending HCP confirmation, question 3).

to.description: Only events whose `timestamp` is at or before this instant: the upper bound of HCP 8.3's date range (the name as in HCP 9.4.12). Inclusive, pending HCP confirmation (questions 29 and 30).
